title: Trump hits the road to sell healthcare plan; signs of conservative backing
text: U.S. President Donald Trump turned to his barnstorming strategy on Wednesday to try to build momentum for his first legislative initiative, a healthcare overhaul, holding a massive rally in Nashville, Tennessee, that recalled his campaign events. Back on Capitol Hill, Republican leaders negotiated behind closed doors, held media conferences and gave cable-news interviews as they tried to advance their plan to dismantle the Affordable Care Act, commonly known as Obamacare. After Republican House Speaker Paul Ryan unveiled the new plan last week, fault lines opened within the party, with some conservatives saying it did not go far enough and others rejecting it outright. Trump used campaign-style language in his Wednesday night speech, pledging “to repeal and replace horrible, disastrous Obamacare.” Talking to reporters aboard the presidential plane Air Force One after the rally, Trump was optimistic about his plan's prospects in Congress. “We’re going to come up with something. We always do,” he said. Republicans control both Congress and the White House for the first time in a decade, but the overhaul still faces political battles to be fought by a president new to governing. Before the rally, White House spokesman Sean Spicer told reporters the Trump administration had been in talks with Ryan and congressional leaders and was flooding the media with interviews with administration officials to help move the plan forward. Ryan, the top Republican in the House of Representatives, also kept championing the legislation, saying on cable news he was open to making “improvements and refinements,” but adding “the major components are staying intact.” Later in the evening he told a news conference the House would hold votes on repealing and replacing Obamacare, but he declined to give a timetable. Two House committees approved the bill's provisions without changes last week.

title: DHS Secretary Kelly Creates VOICE Office For Victims of Illegal Alien Criminals
text: The Department of Homeland Security has opened the Victims of Immigration Crime Engagement (VOICE) Office to give victims of crimes committed by illegal aliens more information about the cases and about the perpetrators' deportation proceedings. “There is nothing but goodness in what we’re doing today,” said John Kelly, the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security. “My heart goes out to you. I do understand what you’ve been through,” he told relatives of murder victims on Wednesday. Kelly, whose son was killed while serving in Afghanistan, went on: “These crimes, in many ways, were preventable. But because of years and years of policies complicating immigration and enforcement efforts, and an approach to public safety, there are mothers who will never again receive a Mother’s Day card from a son. There are husbands who will never again kiss their wives. There are children who will never get to graduate from high school. These victims of illegal aliens aren’t data points. They’re people. And they and their families deserve to be treated fairly … While we can never fully heal them, we can give them a voice.” Kelly took no questions after the briefing and shook hands with the families. The department has also launched the Information and Notification Exchange, an automated, national system that sends automatic updates on changes in custody information for specific illegal aliens charged with or convicted of a crime. It will help victims, families, attorneys, victims' advocates and others navigate the federal immigration system. The system will also automatically send victims and families updates on releasable criminal case information and other changes in custody status. In addition, victims and families will be able to see where an illegal alien is being detained.

title: STEVE SCALISE Throws A Strike At The Nationals Baseball Game
text: House Majority Whip Steve Scalise (R., La.) threw a strike with his ceremonial first pitch at the Washington Nationals' opening-round playoff game Friday night, which also happened to be his birthday. Scalise was shot in the hip and nearly died in June, and he had to throw from a walker, but he had no trouble delivering a perfect pitch to Capitol police special agent David Bailey, who was also injured in the shooting. After taking a bullet on a field in Alexandria, Va., Scalise was visibly happy to be back on the diamond, and afterwards he expressed his gratitude on Twitter, on October 7, 2017: What a memorable birthday! I threw the first pitch at tonight's Nationals vs. Cubs NLDS game! Scalise returned to the House of Representatives last week to a warm welcome from his colleagues, and he expressed thankfulness for his recovery. It's only strengthened my faith in God, and it's really crystallized what shows up as the goodness in people, he said. I got to see that goodness in people, and so while some people might focus on a tragic event and an evil act, to me, all I'll remember are the thousands of acts of kindness and love that came out of this.

title: Sanders supporters fume over Clinton's leaked remarks to Wall Street
text: Supporters of former Democratic presidential candidate Bernie Sanders voiced anger and vindication on Saturday over leaked comments Hillary Clinton made to banks and big business, which appeared to confirm their fears about her support for global trade and her tendency to cozy up to Wall Street. In one of the speeches, Clinton, who needs Sanders' coalition of young and left-leaning voters to carry her to the presidency, pushes for open trade and open borders, and she takes a conciliatory line toward Wall Street, both positions she later retreated from in an effort to capture the popular appeal of Sanders' attacks on trade deals and powerful banks. The excerpts of remarks by the former secretary of state, delivered in 2013 and 2014 at closed-door meetings where audiences paid to attend, were published online on Friday by WikiLeaks, which said they came from the email account of John Podesta, Clinton's campaign chairman. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the speech transcripts. Clinton has previously declined to release any such transcripts. “This is a very clear illustration of why there is a fundamental lack of trust from progressives for Hillary Clinton,” said Tobita Chow, chair of the People's Lobby in Chicago, which endorsed Sanders in the primary election. “The progressive movement needs to make a call to Secretary Clinton to clarify where she stands really on these issues and that’s got to involve very clear renunciations of the positions that are revealed in these transcripts,” Chow said. The revelations were quickly overshadowed by the release of an 11-year-old recording of Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump making lewd comments about women. Clinton has worked hard to build trust with so-called progressives, adopting several of Sanders' positions after she beat him in the primary race.

title: Trump DESPERATE For Celebrities At His Inauguration, So He's Doing This
text: His main qualification to be President of the United States was his celebrity status from hosting his reality TV show, The Apprentice, yet Donald Trump doesn't actually have many contacts among real A-list celebrities. Trump's inability to attract the big names now apparently extends to his upcoming inauguration, where the Trump team is reportedly trying to bribe big names into coming on board out of sheer desperation. One talent manager described being offered access to the administration if he could lure major talent. They said they were in the process of figuring out posts, ambassadorships, and commissions if that was of any interest, he said. Another source also described getting a serious ambassadorship offer, and said he was so shocked by the proposal that he almost dropped the phone. Never in a million years have I heard something so crazy, he said. Both turned the offers down. Trump's team is denying the story, but the whiff of desperation echoes many of the strange things they've already been involved in. Trump is going to have to try very hard to get even half the star power that showed up at President Obama's two inaugurations.

title: Kurds propose joint border deployment as Iraq threatens new military operations
text: Iraq's Kurdish region said on Thursday it had proposed a joint Kurdish-Iraqi deployment, with the participation of U.S.-led international forces, at a strategic crossing into Turkey as part of a compromise aimed at ending its stand-off with Baghdad. The offer was made public hours after the Iraqi armed forces threatened to resume military operations against the Kurds, accusing them of stalling the handover of border control and using negotiations to strengthen their defenses. The central government in Baghdad has cracked down hard on the Kurds since the government of the Kurdish autonomous region held an independence referendum on Sept. 25 that Baghdad considers illegal. Central government forces swiftly took over swathes of Kurdish-held territory last month and have demanded control of all border checkpoints, including the Turkish frontier, which the Kurds have controlled since the Saddam Hussein era. Over the past week, the Kurds have tried to defuse the crisis through negotiations. The Kurdish defense department said the offer of joint control of the frontier was part of a deconfliction proposal made to Baghdad on Oct. 31. Other proposals included a ceasefire on all fronts, continued cooperation in the fight against Islamic State and joint deployments in so-called disputed territories claimed by both the Kurds and the Iraqi central government. The KRG continues to welcome a permanent ceasefire on all fronts, deconfliction and the start of a political dialogue with Baghdad, the Kurdish statement said. Prime Minister Haider al-Abadi suspended military operations against the Kurds on Friday. The two sides have since held talks which Baghdad says cover only technical issues, with political questions off the table unless the Kurds abandon the referendum. Iran and Turkey support Abadi's tough line, fearing that a push for independence could spread to their own Kurdish populations.

title: EU lawmakers ask for 'protection' on Malta visit after threats
text: European Union lawmakers have requested protection for their visit to Malta this week to look into accusations of high-level corruption on the island, citing death threats made against some members of the EU parliament. This month the legislature passed a motion expressing concern about democracy and the rule of law in the EU's smallest state, after the killing of a journalist who had accused some political leaders of graft and money laundering. A group of seven MEPs will visit Malta on Thursday and Friday. In a letter seen by Reuters, Manfred Weber, the German leader of the center-right bloc, wrote to European Parliament President Antonio Tajani on Wednesday asking him to remind the Maltese authorities of their duty to protect the delegation and to allow its members to carry out their duty free from fear. The stark wording of the letter highlighted the strength of feeling in Brussels over recent developments in Malta. It also echoed Tajani's call on Monday for the Polish government to guarantee the safety of MEPs after a far-right protest there over an EU parliament motion on democracy in Poland. Centre-left Maltese Prime Minister Joseph Muscat says Malta does not tolerate crime and has promised justice for the murdered journalist, who had made personal accusations against him as well as against members of the center-right opposition party. Sven Giegold, a German member of the EU parliament's Greens party and a leading campaigner on financial crime who will be part of the delegation, told Reuters he was not very worried but added: I hope the security will be guaranteed.

title: Irving Fields, Composer Who Gave Songs Latin Rhythms, Dies at 101
text: In the middle of the last century, children in certain parts of the Bronx and Brooklyn were often asked to entertain guests with a song called “Miami Beach Rhumba,” an improbable blend of zesty Latin dance rhythms and musical inflections born in the shtetls and ghettos of Eastern Europe. The man who wrote that song was Irving Fields, who died on Saturday at 101 at his home in Manhattan, and his career was as improbable as his songs. In his younger years, Mr. Fields specialized in giving standards a Latin treatment. He and a trio began with an album for Decca Records called “Bagels and Bongos,” which playfully turned melancholy Yiddish chestnuts like “Raisins and Almonds” and “My Yiddishe Momme” into mambos. When the album sold tens of thousands of copies, he recorded a sequel and then went on to Latinize Italian standards (“Pizza and Bongos”), Hawaiian melodies (“Bikinis and Bongos”) and French songs (“Champagne and Bongos”). He also wrote songs, the best known of which was “Miami Beach Rhumba,” a 1946 number about a traveler who sets out for Havana and ends up in the Jewish Riviera of the song’s title. With lyrics by Albert Gamse, including the line “I’ll save Havana for mañana”, it became a fixture of 1950s and ’60s bar mitzvahs. The Latin bandleader Xavier Cugat made it a hit in 1947, and Tito Puente recorded it too. Fifty years later, Woody Allen used it in his film “Deconstructing Harry.” (John Camacho is also credited with a hand in writing it.) Other Fields collaborations included “Managua, Nicaragua,” a hit for Guy Lombardo, and “Chantez, Chantez,” a sprightly tune that Dinah Shore recorded in 1957.

title: Senator Hatch criticizes House's Puerto Rico debt bill
text: A senior Republican senator on Tuesday rejected as “not satisfactory” draft legislation meant to tackle Puerto Rico's fiscal crisis ahead of a looming debt default on May 1, deepening divisions within the party over the complex rescue effort. Orrin Hatch of Utah, who chairs the powerful Senate Finance Committee, told reporters that the draft legislation introduced this month by the House Natural Resources Committee is “not satisfactory and it’s not going to work. And we’re not going to be able to pass it over here” in the Senate. House of Representatives Speaker Paul Ryan and fellow Republican leaders were already struggling to move forward a bill to help Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory, cope with its crippling $70 billion debt. Their efforts have been complicated by opposition from some conservative lawmakers, even as they negotiate details with the Obama administration. Some conservative House Republicans who want to protect creditors' rights have balked at a part of the bill that could let Puerto Rico cut repayments to creditors without their consent, a so-called cram-down debt restructuring. Hatch also wants to protect creditors, but he said the bill must include cram-down authority to make sure more senior bondholders, such as holders of Puerto Rico's constitutionally backed public debt, are better protected. “Let’s face it, you’ve got to protect the preferred creditors. If you don’t do that, I mean, you’re violating the rule of law to begin with,” Hatch said, adding that he is working on a different approach to the legislation. The internal split highlights the complexity of the task facing lawmakers: keeping Puerto Rico's economy intact while also protecting the competing interests of 18 classes of bondholders owed money by the island.
